title: Interpreting Physics in Video World Models
methods: layerwise linear and attentive-MLP probes on the residual stream
IntPhys possible-vs-impossible classification and synthetic Kubric ball dataset with ground-truth velocity/acceleration
subspace overlap analysis with random baselines
iterative probe orthogonalization (nullspace-style) to estimate dimensionality
targeted suppression of local spatiotemporal attention in the emergence zone
multi-direction activation steering of decoded motion direction
question: Where and in what form do video world-model encoders represent physical variables, and are these compact physics-engine-like states or distributed task-specific codes?
key_findings: Possible-vs-impossible probe accuracy jumps from ~50% to ~85-95% at about one-third depth in all V-JEPA 2 sizes ('Physics Emergence Zone'), peaks mid-network and degrades toward the output; smaller VideoMAE-v2 variants do not show reliable emergence.

Speed and acceleration magnitude are decodable from early layers, while motion direction becomes accessible only at the emergence zone; acceleration is decodable without an explicit velocity intermediate.
Direction and possible-impossible judgments occupy nearly orthogonal subspaces (task-specific, not shared latent physics).

Suppressing local spatiotemporal attention in the emergence zone drops direction R2 from 0.97 to 0.14 and IntPhys probe accuracy from 78.3% to 61.7%, while ImageNet probe accuracy barely moves (33.7% to 33.1%) (Table 2).

Direction is a circular population code needing ~40-50 orthogonal probe directions (up to 80 near the output); single-direction steering leaves >80 degree error, while steering across all probe directions at layer 8 gives <0.5 degree error.

benchmarks: control tasks: CLEVRER counting, ImageNet, Something-Something-v2
evidence.scale: multiple model scales; dataset sizes in appendix (not extracted)
evidence.statistics: partial: random-subspace baselines for overlaps; no CIs on probe accuracies in the parts read
evidence.baselines: random subspaces, control tasks, spatial-only vs temporal-only attention ablations

causal_validation: Yes: attention-locality ablations with task-specific controls and multi-dimensional activation steering of the decoded direction (steering effect measured on probe readouts, not on downstream predictions).
limitations_stated: Only encoder-based masked-objective video transformers; autoregressive or diffusion video models may differ.
Covers coarse spatiotemporal reasoning, not contact dynamics or force inference.
Characterizes accessibility and coarse causal influence, not a full circuit; synthetic ball data may not reflect natural video.
critique: Methodologically strong template for robotics interpretability: layer sweeps with control tasks, dimensionality estimates via iterative nullspace, and ablations with task-specific controls.

Key lesson for VLA steering papers: physically meaningful variables may be high-dimensional population codes that single-direction steering cannot move; failures of single-vector steering in VLAs should not be read as absence of the variable.
Steering success is measured on the same probes used to define the subspace, so it shows the subspace controls the probe readout, not that the model's predictions follow.
Relevant to world-action models (2606.01095) and to the position paper's (2606.30686) question of whether physical variables are represented at all; V-JEPA-style encoders are used in some WAMs.
one_line: Physical information in V-JEPA 2 and VideoMAE-v2 appears abruptly about one-third into the network, motion direction is a distributed circular code that needs dozens of dimensions to steer, and local spatiotemporal attention there is causally needed for physics judgments.
